long_biography.plain_text:
Mentasti joined San Pellegrino’s management in the 1930s and spent more than twenty years as an executive and director before becoming president and chief executive in 1958. After his father-in-law Ezio Granelli’s death, he oversaw mineral water, bottled beverages, Acqua Panna and related chemical-pharmaceutical businesses. The group grew into a large national producer, while product innovation and acquisitions extended its market reach.

His interests also shaped the northern Sardinian coast. Mentasti participated in the early planning of the Costa Smeralda and bought land around Porto Cervo before the resort’s development. In 1967 he co-founded its non-profit sailing club, helping establish an institution that became prominent in international competition. He also supported employee welfare, universities, youth organisations and environmental stewardship through a model agricultural estate in Lombardy.

uncertainties: The corrected Croce del Sud relationship resolves the owner as Giuseppe ‘Kerry’ Mentasti at very high confidence. MareOnline identifies the vessel’s 1957 transfer to Mentasti, the Historical Diving Society independently names it as his vessel, the Yacht Club Costa Smeralda links both person and vessel to Costa Smeralda history, and the Quirinale corroborates the same San Pellegrino executive.

The upstream relationship begins in 1977, whereas independent historical sources say Croce del Sud passed to Mentasti in 1957. The dossier does not alter vessel chronology; the discrepancy should be reviewed separately from biography enrichment.

The upstream Alive mortality status is stale. A Historical Diving Society obituary published in October 2001 reports that Mentasti died on May 4 at age 93 and directly anchors the notice to both Croce del Sud and San Pellegrino, supporting the correction to Deceased and the 2001 death year.

L’Unione Sarda gives 1908 as Mentasti’s birth year, and death at age 93 on May 4, 2001 is consistent with that year. No strong source supplied the exact birth day or month, so only the year is proposed and its confidence is reduced to high.

‘Kerry’ was a journalistic pseudonym that remained attached to Mentasti, not an evidenced legal middle name. It is used as a durable public alias in narrative fields but is not proposed as middle_names.

Marriage / family transfer is selected because Mentasti entered the established Granelli enterprise as Ezio Granelli’s son-in-law and succeeded him, while financial reporting later identifies the Mentasti family as controller. Public sources do not establish the exact legal instrument by which shares passed, so the summary avoids claiming a testamentary inheritance.

Operator is selected because Mentasti served as president and chief executive for four decades and made documented acquisition, product and distribution decisions. The active mandate is better supported than a passive heir or family-shareholder relationship.

Food & Beverage is retained as primary industry because it is the latest strongly documented principal operating platform. The family sold its controlling stake shortly before Mentasti’s death, but no strong source establishes how proceeds were reinvested or identifies a later dominant private industry.

Beverage manufacturing is the sole proposed tag because it exactly captures the closed-taxonomy, long-term operating mandate. Pharmaceutical operations, property development, agriculture, sailing and diving were material contextual dimensions but are not independently established as principal wealth specialisms under the approved tag contracts.

No authenticated personal LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website, canonical Wikipedia biography or dedicated Forbes profile was established. The Quirinale honour page and Yacht Club institutional histories are evidence sources, not personal social-profile proposals.

Neither biography names the current vessel, gives ownership chronology or specifications, discusses the family’s sale price, or depends on current valuations. Sailing-club and Costa Smeralda work remains because it is a durable, independently documented part of Mentasti’s public identity.
